chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Abu Isma'il al-Sarraj from Harun ibn Harizah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He said to me regarding the Prayer of Gratitude: 'When Allah, Exalted and Glorious, bestows a favor upon you, then pray two rak'ahs. Recite in the first Surah Al-Fatiha and 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad', and in the second Surah Al-Fatiha and 'Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun'. And say in the first rak'ah during your bowing and prostration: 'All praise is for Allah, thanks, thanks and praise.' And say in the second rak'ah during your bowing and prostration: 'All praise is for Allah who answered my supplication and granted my request.'
ai.seo_question: What are the specific prayers and Surahs to recite in the Shia Prayer of Gratitude (Salat al-Shukr)?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides the precise ritual framework for Salat al-Shukr, emphasizing the integration of specific Surahs with unique dhikr in ruku and sujud to manifest deep gratitude. It highlights the Shia scholarly tradition of linking physical acts of worship with verbal acknowledgments of divine favor, reinforcing the concept that gratitude is both a spiritual state and a prescribed act of devotion.
